status_scope: Comparison review complete. Captures retain recorded visibility and lighting limits.

images.observation: Boiler face, gauge and overhead fittings retain comparable coverage. The right wall still cuts into the room.
Case glazing, wood floor and back door remain comparable. Dim closed shelving limits the book detail.
North day parapet, tank supports and glazing remain comparable. The ground is dark.
North dusk facade windows retain their pattern. The roof remains dark.
North street panes and their reveals remain visible. Brick faces are dark.
Northeast day recessed court and roof profile remain comparable against the dark ground.
Northeast dusk recess and pane rhythm retain their outline. Lower ground is dark.
Northeast street framing preserves the recessed center and regular window spacing.
South day dormer outlines and the warm near roof stock are visible.
South dusk dormer forms and glazed rows remain visible against a dark facade.
South street view preserves the dormer silhouette and regular facade panes.
Southeast day roof and parapet border read clearly over the shaded court.
Southeast dusk retains the warm roof and window groups. The ground is dark.
Southeast street balcony and brick facade retain the same composition.
Southwest day retains the tank, antenna supports and distinctive parapet. Traffic changed at the lower edge.
Southwest dusk roof hardware and surrounding windows stay clear against the warmer street.
Southwest street court recess and flanking pane rows remain legible.
West day retains the raised roof edge, tank and centered facade projection.
West dusk retains the warm roof plane and shadow from the tank. The street stays dark.
West street cornice and window pattern remain visible, with the lower facade outside frame.
East roof is sky dominated. The nearest rooftop fittings remain along the lower edge.
The first ground-edge view retains the curb and long grade. The far basin is still dark.
The second ground-edge view preserves the steep grade and adjacent building corner.
The dark ground seam and near brick building remain distinct. The distant blocks still sit in haze.
The lit right-hand block and darker foreground stock maintain their separation.
The bridge crowns remain readable on the right. The low new skyline appears left of them.
Traffic differs in the foreground, including the near car and cyclist. The street opening and both facades still read.
The landward canal view remains dark. The bulkhead has low contrast at this angle.
The original rail-cut overlook remains faint. This view alone does not show the switcher clearly.
River haze and the distant facade bands remain comparable. The foreground bank is dark.
The rooftop window, metal mast and nearby masonry remain distinct.
The close panes, red sign and right-side steel framing remain readable.
Cool panes retain the tall cabinet and low furniture silhouettes beside the separate warm lower panes. The dark foreground wall and the facade shadow continue to limit the left side.
Gray surrounds, brick arches and stepped trim retain their profiles. Warm foreground panes remain distinct from cool center panes, with low-contrast detail in the trim recesses.

The brick face, awning, curved streetlamp and lit slatted blind remain legible against the distant roofs. A dark olive vehicle occupies part of the incoming lower-left street and masks some foreground detail.

Cornices, arched surrounds, roof profiles and warm and cool glazing remain comparable. Incoming vehicles intrude from both lower corners and the right vehicle covers part of the ground-level frontage.
The blue sky, pale cloud bands, antenna lines and tank tops retain comparable forms. The elevated aim leaves most roof surfaces below the crop.
Pale clouds and softened distant silhouettes retain the fog appearance. The near tank profiles and thin mast wires still read along the lower edge. Distant surface detail remains obscured.
Muted gray sky and the warmer horizon retain the same gradient. Near tanks and wires remain identifiable while distant roofs recede into low-contrast silhouettes.
The bridge truss, tanks and antenna lines remain distinct. A low hazy mass appears beyond the nearby roof line just left of the incoming truss. Deep roof shadows and distance limit material detail.
Wall tile, upper paint, vertical strip and the partial toilet look comparable. The named service connection remains outside the visible crop.
Dark near brick occupies both views. The fixture remains hidden and this view supplies no visual inspection of it.
The warm pendant, floorboards, central table, radiator and left equipment table remain visible. The companion overlaps the right shelving and the nearest instrument is cropped by the lower edge.
The warm circular lamp falloff, tile line and curtain remain visible. The framing and companion show only part of the toilet and limit inspection beyond the lit wall.
The radiator, blinds, round table, workbench and resident remain visible under comparable warm lighting. The companion masks part of the right shelving.

The warm wall and floorboards, window, table and radiator remain visible. The loose foreground chair is absent in the incoming frame, exposing more floor. The companion still overlaps the table at right.
The upper cupboard, kettle, sink and visible pipework retain comparable detail around the warm light on the wall. The companion masks part of the sink and right edge.

The open enclosure, upper connections and fuse faces remain identifiable. The incoming inside door and lower conduit are darker than before, while the wall and right shelf are still lit enough to distinguish.
The brass mailbox grid, dark open slots and lower letter slot remain visible. Dim wall lighting and the tight view limit smaller lettering and surrounding structure.
The radiator ribs, brass fittings, blinds and adjacent tabletop remain visible under warm light. The dress form at left and lower framing still obscure part of the installation.
The cage rails, drive housing, wall sign and stair opening remain identifiable under the warm overhead lamp. The shadowed housing and cage limit inspection of finer drive details.
The tank body, cap, access rail and legs remain comparable against the roof and distant facades. The near support frame and lower roof stay dark, limiting finer surface comparison.

The street-facing masonry, upper trim and lit panes remain legible. An incoming vehicle occupies much of the lower-right foreground and the left vehicle still partly covers the road and ground-level edge.
The terminal and its green reflection on the table remain visible with the floorboards, sofa and wall frame. The near cabinet and oblique framing still limit inspection of the far side.
The tiled corner, wall trim and partial toilet retain comparable appearance. The deeper named service components remain outside the visible crop.
The saturated residue pool and raised pieces remain clear in the lamp circle beneath the radiator. The perimeter floor and fittings remain in shadow and the companion partly covers the right side.
The upright stock, radiator ribs and floorboards remain distinguishable inside the lamp circle. Dark edges and the companion still obscure adjacent fittings.
The toaster, crumbs, pale kettle and surrounding work surfaces retain comparable detail in the warm interior light. The right edge remains partially cropped.
The station plate and small gold dial remain visible against the dim textured wall. The cut-off pale sign at lower right and low ambient light limit context outside the fixture.
